# Pain Point

`sales.obj.core.pain_point` · v1.0.0 · **draft** · scope **core**

> A specific problem the buyer experiences, carrying a cost and an owner. The discriminator is ownership, not severity: a pain with no owner is an observation, and observations do not fund purchases. "Reporting is manual" is an observation; "the Head of Finance spends three days a month rebuilding the board pack and is measured on close time" is a pain point, because there is a person, a number and a consequence. The second discriminator is against Business Need — pain is what hurts now, need is what better looks like. Sellers who collect pain and never convert it into a need have a compelling story and nothing to be measured against after the sale.


Also called: `Problem`, `Challenge`, `Identified Pain`, `Business Problem`

## Constraints

- **`pp.cost_requires_a_basis`** annual_cost may not be asserted without cost_basis. Anunattributed number is indefensible in the review it was written for.
- **`pp.owner_must_be_a_person`** owner_ref points to a named individual, never to a teamor a function. Teams do not approve spend.
- **`pp.no_pain_no_proposal`** A proposal must reference at least one pain point in thebuyer's own language.
- **`pp.hypothesised_is_not_identified`** A hypothesised pain may not be reported to thebuyer as something they told us. Being corrected on this costs the discovery relationship outright.


## Business rules

- **`pp.no_owner_no_business_case`** A pain point with no owner_ref must not be used as the primary justification in a proposal. Procurement asks whose budget line this comes from, and "the team" is not an answer anyone can sign.

- **`pp.vendor_estimated_cost_must_be_labelled`** Where cost_basis is vendor_estimated or assumed, annual_cost must be labelled as our estimate wherever it appears. An unlabelled vendor number that the buyer's finance team disproves discredits every other number in the document.

- **`pp.tolerable_pain_with_a_workaround_names_do_nothing`** When current_workaround is present and severity is trivial or tolerable, "do nothing" must be recorded as the leading competitor rather than leaving the competitor field empty.

- **`pp.price_objection_without_a_cost`** A price objection raised against an uncosted pain means the buyer is comparing our price to zero. The correct response is to quantify, not to discount.

- **`pp.single_source_pain_is_an_opinion`** A pain with corroboration_count of one may not raise deal confidence on its own, whatever the seniority of the person who said it.
- **`pp.owner_departure_invalidates_the_pain`** When champion_change is observed, owner_ref must be re-verified before the pain is treated as live. Pains do not transfer with roles; accountability does not either, until someone says so.

## Actions

- **Ask who is accountable for the cost** (human) — Convertsan observation into a pain point. One question, and it is skipped in most discovery calls because it feels blunt.
- **Build the cost model together** (human) — Movescost_basis from vendor_estimated to jointly_calculated. A number the buyer helped produce is one they will defend internally.
- **Cost the existing workaround** (human) — Prices 'donothing' explicitly, which is the only way to compete with it.
- **Test for an external deadline** (human) — Separatesa real date from a preference. Two slips means the answer was always preference.
- **Test the pain with a second stakeholder** (human) — Raises corroboration_count, or reveals that one person's irritation was mistaken for an organisational problem.
- **Re-approach a dormant pain at the fiscal turn** (human) — The highest-conversion outbound available, because discovery is already done and the competitor's is not.


## Evidence

- **document** · 9500 bp — The buyer's own written business case or RFP problemstatement. They wrote it for an internal audience, so it is what they actually believe.
- **meeting_transcript** · 8500 bp — Verbatim description with an owner claimingit. The richest source, and currently unmined.
- **call_recording** · 8000 bp — Same content, weaker attribution when severalpeople speak.
- **email** · 7000 bp — Written by the buyer, so quotable — but email under-reportspain, since nobody types their worst problem to a vendor.
- **crm** · 5500 bp — Prior discovery notes. Decays fast and is written invendor language.
- **website** · 3500 bp — Annual reports and job adverts. Good for hypothesising,never for asserting.
- **derived** · 3000 bp — Inferred from commercial signals arriving afterthe pain. Corroborating only.


## Metrics

- **owned_pain_rate** (percent) — Share of pains carrying an owner_ref. The clearestsingle measure of discovery quality.
- **quantification_rate** (percent) — Share carrying a buyer-supplied cost basis.
- **time_to_quantify** (days) — First mention to quantified cost. Long tails herepredict deals that die at the business-case stage.
- **corroboration_depth** (count) — Average independent confirmations per pain.
- **do_nothing_loss_rate** (percent) — Share of losses to no-decision. Reads directlyon status_quo_strength.
- **pain_reuse_at_renewal** (percent) — Share of renewals where the original painis still the stated reason to stay.


## Examples

- **Support triage costs 40 hours a week and the Head of Support carries the SLA** — Theshape you want: statement, frequency, cost, owner, and a metric the owner is measured on. Everything downstream has something to attach to.
- **"We're growing fast"** — THE CLASSIC MISCLASSIFICATION. Context recorded as pain.Nobody owns growth, nothing costs anything, and no proposal can be measured against it. It gets logged because it feels like momentum.
- **"Our reporting is manual"** — Real, common, and unowned. Until someone is accountablefor the hours, this funds nothing — it is the second most-logged non-pain after the one above.
- **SOC 2 evidence collection before an audit dated in March** — Compliance category, datedcompelling event, personally liable owner. The fastest-closing shape in B2B and the one where discount pressure is weakest.
- **The CTO finds the integration painful; nobody else mentions it** — corroboration_countof one. One senior person's irritation is not an organisational pain and will not survive their next reorganisation, however loudly it is stated.

## Metadata

> Eleven inference patterns: five executable against the substrate today, six blocked. The executable five all read pain indirectly, through the commercial reactions that follow it — objections, discount pressure, silence, freezes — because the substrate has eighteen observation kinds for how a buyer reacts to a price and none for a buyer describing a problem. The single highest-value signal gap is therefore obs_kind `pain_stated` with a verbatim statement span (L2): it unblocks three patterns here directly, is the precondition for `derived.pain_topic_cluster`, and without it the discovery half of the sales motion is permanently invisible to the engine. Second in line is obs_kind `accountability_stated`, which populates owner_ref — the one field this entire object turns on.
